messages:
security-bot: [Alert] Unusual SSO pattern detected: 26 accounts affected in ~4m, high failure rate + short inter-event intervals. score=86
Alex G: saw the alert. looks like staccato login waves from multiple geos. users are getting lockouts and MFA prompts stacking up.
Mira P: can we get the top IPs + whether any logins succeeded? and which apps (console vs api)?
Samir K: running quick auth query now, pulling top IPs and success/fail counts.
Samir K: ```sql
SELECT ip, count(*) as attempts, sum(success::int) as successes, min(ts) as first, max(ts) as last
FROM auth.events
WHERE ts >= 1872499940 AND event_type = 'sso'
GROUP BY ip
ORDER BY attempts DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
Samir K: quick results: 10.10.45.2 (422 attempts, 3 successes), 203.12.5.90 (300 attempts, 0 successes), 45.77.2.1 (128 attempts, 0 successes). Most target console logins.
Kevin L: 3 successes from 10.10.45.2 — which accounts were they? redact sensitive details in-thread.
Samir K: affected accounts (summarized): jdoe, infra-bot, marketing-sync. sending full list in #sec-ops-private DM. infra-bot looks like a service account — marking for immediate token rotation.
oncall-ops: propose blocking 10.10.45.0/24 at edge and rate-limiting 203.12.5.90. any objections?
Alex G: block and rate-limit. also force global session revoke and rotate tokens for the service accounts that had successes from 10.10.45.2.
Mira P: +1. also temporarily require MFA re-prompt for console auths for 1h.
oncall-ops: executing containment steps now. commands:
```bash
# block IP range
firewallctl block 10.10.45.0/24 --reason "staccato login wave"
# throttle suspicious IP
wafctl rate-limit add 203.12.5.90/32 10/min --reason "auth abuse"
# revoke sessions globally
authctl revoke-sessions --scope all --reason "suspicious logins"
```
oncall-ops: firewall block applied, rate-limit active, revoke jobs queued. ETA ~45s.
security-bot: additional signal: 12 MFA push failures within 2m, pattern consistent with MFA fatigue/prompt attacks.
Alex G: likely automated prompt attempts. we should notify impacted users that we've rotated sessions and they may need to re-login. drafting user comms now.
Mira P: creating incident (sev2). include affected accounts, IPs, containment actions, and follow-ups: audit log export, service account key rotations, KMS key check.
Samir K: exporting raw auth logs to locked S3 bucket for forensic analysis: s3://redwood-sec/incident-1872500000 (access controlled).
Kevin L: preliminary postmortem checklist: 1) tighten RBAC for service accounts; 2) enforce short-lived keys and token lifetimes; 3) add detector for staccato login pattern; 4) review KMS access and rotation policy for service keys.
oncall-ops: confirm no additional successful logins after revoke. monitoring telemetry for anomalies.
Alex G: good containment. assigning owners: Mira = incident lead, Samir = forensics/logs, Kevin = policy/hardening, oncall-ops = edge/config changes. ETA for initial incident report: 2h.
Mira P: noted. I'll also open a support ticket for any internal teams seeing issues. cc @security-communications.
security-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-18725. link: https://redwood/incidents/INC-2026-18725
Alex G: :thumbsup: keep concise updates here. escalate to execs if we see data exfil or lateral access.
oncall-ops: monitoring window 1h, will post update at +30m.
